title: CS Cataloger: Priority Lens and Solution Readout for Enterprise Feature Requests
text:
CS Cataloger: Priority Lens and Solution Readout for Enterprise Feature Requests

description:
Problem: CS and Sales receive high-volume, heterogeneous enterprise feature asks (non-bug). There is inconsistent initial scoping across reps: some include budgets and infra preferences, others only a one-line ask. This variance slows PD/ENG review and causes repeated clarifying cycles. Goal: build a lightweight 'Cataloger' intake artifact and priority lens that standardizes first-pass scoping (value, cost-driver flags, infra fit, compliance needs) so PMs can (1) fast-track highest-econ requests, (2) route low-effort wins to Solutions/SE for field delivery, and (3) identify items needing cross-team architecture review.

initial_scope_sketch:
MVP will be a 1-page form (prefill when possible from SFDC notes) plus a scoring sheet. Scoring weights: ARR(40), Implementation Effort(25), Strategic Fit(20), Compliance Complexity(15). Implementation effort will map to rough eng points (1,3,8,13) for quicker economic math. We will include a checkbox for 'requires on-prem or VPC' which will trigger a Dedicated/Private ops consult. MVP excludes automated sync to Linear (manual create) but includes a copy/paste summary block optimised for creating a PM ticket.

acceptance_criteria:
A standardized intake template (Cataloger) exists and can be filled by CS/Sales in <=20 minutes
Priority lens applied to 50 recent asks produces a top-10 list that aligns with GTM/PM expectations in >=80% of cases
Template fields capture at minimum: business outcome, rough ARR estimate, expected monthly QPS, preferred deployment (hosted/dedicated/private), data sensitivity, timeline, must-have vs nice-to-have, suggested engineering owner
A playbook for routing (SE/solutions, PM-run spike, architecture review) is documented and tested in one CS->PM handoff
Initial automation: a Google Form + simple spreadsheet with calculated score using weights (value, customer tier, compliance) is deployed for a pilot

decision_log:
2025-02-14: Agreed to prioritize quick-economic clarity over exhaustive technical detail for first pass (decision by Priya, Ethan, and Nina from Solutions).
2025-02-20: Chose scoring weights above after calibration on 20 historical asks (score produced in 16/20 cases matching senior PM prioritization).
2025-02-25: Scoped MVP to Google Form + Sheet for fastest iteration; postponed building Linear integration to Post-MVP.
2025-03-01: Added explicit 'data residency / regulatory' field after Legal flag in pilot feedback (reduces re-clarification by solutions).

comments:
2025-02-13 - Ethan Caldwell: Spun up an internal prototype form and ran it against 12 recent inbound asks; results attached to drive link below. Observations: reps often skip ARR but can provide 'deal size band' which is good enough.
2025-02-18 - Priya Menon: Reviewed prototype outputs — recommend adding a required 'expected QPS' field (even a band) for routing to Dedicated capacity stakeholders.
2025-02-21 - Nina Park (Solutions): For 'requires on-prem' flows we need a parallel checklist for procurement and legal; suggest a tag that auto-triggers a Solutions assignment.
2025-02-28 - Engineering reviewer (Alexei Orlov): Quick note — map the 'Implementation Effort' bands to a pre-defined spike template so PMs can request a 5-day scoping spike when needed.
2025-03-02 - Data Privacy (Maria Santos): Confirmed that the 'data sensitivity' field needs three levels (public/internal/regulated) and that regulated should require a follow-up with Security; updated playbook accordingly.

open_questions:
How strict should we be about ARR estimates? (free-form vs banded vs required)
Should the Cataloger live in Forms, a lightweight internal app, or embedded in SFDC? Trade-offs: friction vs discoverability.
What SLA should PMs commit to for initial response after submission? (48hrs recommended by Solutions)
How to surface historical similar asks to avoid duplicate work? (manual tag vs automated similarity scoring)
Who owns the 'deployability' decision for marginal asks that could be served by hosted + cache optimizations versus Dedicated?

next_steps:
Pilot run: Collect 30 incoming asks via the Cataloger form over 3 weeks (owner: Ethan)
Implement scoring sheet with automated top-10 extraction and weekly digest to PM inbox (owner: Priya)
Create Solutions routing rule for 'on-prem/VPC' and 'regulated' tags (owner: Nina)
Draft short training doc and 10-min demo for CS reps; include 'how to estimate ARR band' heuristics (owner: Product Ops)
Revisit Linear integration and automation after pilot; estimate for integration in Cycle 42 if pilot meets acceptance criteria (owner: Eng PM)
Post-pilot retro and scoreboard alignment with Sales leadership (date target: 2025-04-01)
